question.text: Tungabhadra Buyout II (Cat II): Committed INR 200 cr (fully called). Terminal NAV INR 330 cr. Hurdle 8% compounded. 5-yr tenure. Carry 20% WITHOUT catch-up. Compute the residual profit (above hurdle) and the GP carry.

answer.text: Residual INR 36.1 cr; GP carry INR 7.22 cr
Residual INR 130.0 cr; GP carry INR 26.0 cr
Residual INR 46.9 cr; GP carry INR 26.0 cr
Residual INR 36.1 cr; GP carry INR 26.0 cr

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Hurdle at 5 yr: INR 200 x (1.08)^5 = INR 293.87 cr, so hurdle return = INR 93.87 cr. Total profit = INR 130 cr. Residual above hurdle = INR 130 - 93.87 = INR 36.13 cr. NO catch-up means GP gets 20% of residual = 20% x INR 36.13 = INR 7.23 crore. **The Trap:** B ignores the hurdle entirely (GP carry = 20% x total profit); C has wrong residual base (uses simple 8% x 5 = 40% hurdle = INR 80 cr, so residual INR 50 cr, carry INR 10 cr — still wrong match); D mixes right residual with wrong carry math. **Cross-Exam Context:** Chapter 6 no-catch-up scenario (Example 6.5(a)) uses this exact pattern. XIX-C tests variants with 20% and different hurdles. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** No-catch-up waterfalls shift GP economics dramatically — the GP earns carry only on the ABOVE-HURDLE slug. At modest-return vintages this can halve GP take. If fund-raising is competitive, propose 100% catch-up; if LPs are sticky and cost-sensitive, concede to no-catch-up.
